section_1.title: Can your course fees be covered?
section_1.description: Covers your full tuition fees up to £9,250/yr (or £6,000+ for private/some providers). Paid directly to the provider — you never touch the money.

section_2.title: Key details about Tuition Loans
section_2.description: The tuition fee loan ensures your course fees are paid upfront so you don't face upfront costs.

cards.title: Direct Payment
cards.description: SFE pays the loan straight to the university or college in three instalments per year after your attendance is confirmed.

cards.title: Designation Check
cards.description: The loan is only paid if your specific course and provider are officially SFE-designated for that year.

cards.title: Previous Study rules
cards.description: If you have studied at higher education level before, it can reduce your available years of tuition fee support. Speak to an adviser.

faqs.q: Do I have to pay it back?
faqs.a: Yes, it is part of your student loan balance, but you only repay it after you graduate and earn above the £25,000 income threshold.

faqs.q: What if my fees are higher?
faqs.a: If you study at a private provider where fees exceed the SFE cap, you may need to pay the difference yourself.
